rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage links balance in creation to justice in human relations, then recalls blessings given to people.
rows.anchor: evrendeki dengeye dikkat çekilmekte, beşerî ilişkilerde de dengenin şart olduğu, bunun ise adaletle sağlanabileceği vurgulanmakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precise movement of celestial bodies is presented as clear evidence of God's power.
rows.anchor: gök cisimlerinin ince bir hesaba bağlı hareket ettiklerinin belirtilmesi öncelikle bunun yüce Allah’ın kudretini gösteren açık kanıtlardan olduğu

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur explains the mention of the sun and moon by their special relevance to people.
rows.anchor: bir yorum da yapılmıştır (İbn Âşûr, XXVII, 235

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur also sees a paired-expression style: people habitually think of the moon and sun together.
rows.anchor: bu sûrede eşli durumlara dikkat çekme üslûbunun kullanıldığı, insanların da ay ve güneşi daima birlikte düşündükleri şeklinde bir yorum da yapılmıştır (İbn Âşûr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the ordered creation exists for people, they should order life responsibly and prepare for the coming Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: insan da hayatını bir hesaba göre düzenlemeli, bir hesap gününün geleceği bilinci içinde olmalı ve kendisini bu hesaba hazırlamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here najm means stemless plants such as grain and grass, although the word can also mean stars; the plant sense is generally accepted.
rows.anchor: necm kelimesi, tahıl ve ot gibi gövdesi olmayan bitkileri ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration of trees and plants means their involuntary submission to God's laws; human beings can consciously revere God and obey, which gives their choice special dignity.
rows.anchor: Ağaçların ve diğer bitkilerin secde etmesi, bunların Allah’ın yasalarına iradî olmaksızın boyun eğmelerini ifade etmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky may mean the vast cosmic space containing galaxies and celestial bodies moving in an ordered way.
rows.anchor: milyarlarca galaksi ve gök cisminin içinde yer aldığı ve belli bir düzene göre hareket ettiği kozmik uzayın kastedildiği söylenebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the sky can mean its literal height above us or a metaphorical spiritual elevation.
rows.anchor: bize nisbetle yüksekte olması yahut mecazî anlamda düşünülüp mânevî bir yüksekliğe sahip olması şeklinde yorumlanabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either reading points to God's supreme majesty and the fact that only God deserves worship.
rows.anchor: Her iki mâna, bizi, bunu sağlayan Allah Teâlâ’nın yüceler yücesi olduğu, secde ve kulluk edilmeye lâyık başka mâbud bulunmadığı gerçeğine götürür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mizan can mean balance, measure, weighing relative weights, a weighing instrument, or scales, depending on context.
rows.anchor: “denge, ölçü, eşyanın birbirine nispetle ağırlığını tartma, tartı aleti, terazi” mânalarına gelen mîzân kelimesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first occurrence of mizan suggests the universal balance law that allows the cosmos and all its processes to function as an ordered system.
rows.anchor: Yüce Allah evrende denge kanununu koymuştur; bütün varlık ve oluşlar arasında, evrenin belirli bir sistem dahilinde yürümesini sağlayan bir genel denge mevcuttur

rows.speaker: Taberî ve İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Many exegetes understand mizan here as justice, including Tabari and Ibn Atiyya.
rows.anchor: “adalet” anlamının kastedildiği kanaatindedir (meselâ bk. Taberî, XXVII, 118; İbn Atıyye, V, 224)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion, the divinely given laws for a humane life, manifests balance; justice means putting everything in its proper place, rejecting false divinity and giving each rights-holder their due.
rows.anchor: Bunların özü, genellikle kısaca “her şeyi lâyık olduğu yere koymak” diye tanımlanan adalet ilkesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mizan in verse 8 means this religious and ethical order, since people are told not to violate it or deviate from balance.
rows.anchor: 8. âyetteki mîzan kelimesi bu anlamda olmalıdır; zira burada mîzanın ihlâl edilmemesi, dengeden sapılmaması istenmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice is the basic principle for preserving balance, while fair conduct in concrete human affairs requires care, good-faith judgment, and full effort.
rows.anchor: Beşerî ilişkiler bakımından bunun adı “hakkaniyet”tir. Bunu belirlemede kişilere düşen, takdir yetkisini iyi niyet esasına dayalı olarak kullanmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For duties toward God, justice is realized by following revelation without adding anything of one's own to religion.
rows.anchor: kişinin dine kendisinden bir şey katmadan ilâhî bildirime uygun davranmasıyla mümkündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of qist, meaning fairness, with weighing and scales shows that justice and universal balance must be enacted in lived situations.
rows.anchor: “hakkaniyet” anlamına gelen “kıst” kelimesine yer verilmesi burada vezin ve mîzan kelimelerinin adalet ilkesinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not diminish the measure can also mean acting so that one's deeds do not tip the afterlife scales against oneself.
rows.anchor: her bir olayla ilgili uygulamanın yani bütün davranışlarımızın âhiretteki teraziyi aleyhimize çevirmeyecek biçimde olması gerektiği şeklinde de yorumlanabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The real scales reflect cosmic attraction, while scales have long symbolized justice and concretely establish fair exchange; these links support related senses of mizan.
rows.anchor: el terazisinin evrendeki cazibe (çekim) kanununun bir sonucu olarak bu işlevini yerine getirebiliyor olması, eski zamanlardan beri insanların adaleti temsil etmek üzere teraziyi sembol yapmaları

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes three contextual senses: the weighing instrument, the act of weighing, and the thing weighed.
rows.anchor: Râzî de bu kelimenin konumuz olan âyetlerde üç ayrı mânada kullanıldığı kanaatindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anam covers all living beings, but the verse should be read as making earth habitable for life while keeping humanity as its primary purpose, in line with the passage's theme of human responsibility.
rows.anchor: enâm, canlı varlıkların tamamını kapsayan bir kelimedir; fakat başka âyetlerde yeryüzünde bulunan bütün varlıkların insanın emrine verildiği açıkça ifade edildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kimm, the singular of akmam, means the early husk or covering of a date fruit; the translation uses budding based on this sense.
rows.anchor: kimm, “hurma meyvesinin ilk aşamadaki kapçığı” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the alternative singular kumm, the word can include a tree's fibers, pits, and coverings such as branches and bark.
rows.anchor: Diğer tekili kümm esas alındığında ise ağacın “lifleri, çekirdekleri, dal ve kabuk gibi örtüleri” bu kelimenin kapsamına girer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation sees the two word senses as pointing respectively to the future crop and to produce already formed after successive stages.
rows.anchor: Bir yoruma göre birinci anlamda ileride oluşacak ürüne, ikincisinde ise değişik aşamaların ardından ürünün meydana gelmiş bulunduğuna işaret edilmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation values the palm buds because their cluster is important and makes harvesting easier.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir yoruma göre hurma ağacı açısından tomurcukların oluşturduğu salkım çok önemlidir, ürün toplamayı kolaylaştırır

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Some commentators understand the phrase as drawing attention to the date palm's pleasing appearance.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirler ise burada estetik görünüme, göze hitap eden güzelliğe işaret bulunduğu kanaatindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same word in Fussilat 41:47 refers to fruit splitting its husk and more generally to early fruit coverings or seed shells.
rows.anchor: Aynı kelime Fussılet sûresinin 47. âyetinde meyvenin ürün vermesi için kabuğunu çatlatması bağlamında

rows.speaker: Râzî, İbn Âşûr ve Elmalılı
rows.claim: Although several readings of the sprouting grains are offered, commentators generally take them as cereals of special importance to human nutrition.
rows.anchor: genellikle insanların beslenmelerinde özel önemi haiz olan tahıl türü bitkilerin kastedildiği kabul edilir (Râzî, XXIX, 93-94; İbn Âşûr, XXVII, 242; Elmalılı, VII, 4667)

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Rayhan can mean fragrant plants or provision; Tabari prefers provision and identifies the staple grains as intended.
rows.anchor: Taberî bu yorumu tercih eder ve temel gıda maddesi olan hububatın kastedildiğini belirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah condemns denying God's blessings, whether one denies that something is a blessing, its attribution to God, or both.
rows.anchor: Nimetin nimet olduğunu veya nimetin Allah’a nisbet edilmesini ya da her ikisini inkâr bu eleştirinin kapsamındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain appears 31 times and addresses two people or groups grammatically, asking which of their Lord's blessings they can deny.
rows.anchor: cümlenin yüklemini oluşturan fiil ve “rabbiniz” tamlamasının tamlananı olan zamir tesniye (ikil) kalıbındadır, yani iki kişiye veya iki gruba hitap edilmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts that the dual address is to humans and jinn, based on the creation of both in verses 14–15, the explicit address in verse 32, and related reports.
rows.anchor: konuya ilişkin rivayetler de dikkate alınarak buradaki hitabın insanlara ve cinlere yönelik olduğu kabul edilir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi suggests the dual may emphatically repeat a singular address to the listener.
rows.anchor: Bunun aslı, tekil hitabın vurgu için aynen tekrarlanması olabilir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi also suggests that the dual could address the two human sexes, men and women.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’ın genellikle muhatap aldığı iki insan cinsine yani erkeklere ve kadınlara hitap edilmiş olması

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur interprets the two addressees as believers and unbelievers, meaning that no human can truly deny God's blessings.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre burada insan cinsinin “inananlar” ve “inkârcılar” şeklindeki iki kategorisine hitap edilmekte, mümin olsun kâfir olsun gerçekte hiçbir insanın Allah’ın nimetlerini inkâr edemeyeceği

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur considers the majority view that the address is to humans and jinn remote, arguing that the Quran came to address humans rather than jinn.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr, müfessirlerin çoğunluğunun burada insanlara ve cinlere hitap edildiği şeklindeki yorumunu uzak bir ihtimal olarak görür; çünkü Kur’an cinlere değil insanlara hitap etmek için gelmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haqqa derives from haqq, which means to be real, fixed, true, necessary, to actualize something, or to know it certainly; haqq is often contrasted with falsehood.
rows.anchor: Hak ise sözlükte, “gerçek, sabit ve doğru olmak, gerekmek; bir şeyi gerçekleştirmek; bir şeyi kesin olarak bilmek” gibi mânalara gelmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Resurrection is called al-Haqqa because it certainly occurs and reveals the real value and consequences of people's earthly deeds.
rows.anchor: insanlar dünyada yapıp ettiklerinin gerçek değerini kavrayacakları ve sonuçlarını görecekleri için ona da “Hâkka” ismi verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first three verses convey the event's magnitude and severity and show that its timing cannot be known.
rows.anchor: Sûrenin ilk üç âyeti gerek üslûp gerekse anlam olarak kıyamet olayının büyüklüğüne ve şiddetine işaret ettiği gibi ne zaman meydana geleceğinin bilinemeyeceğini de göstermektedir

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu
rows.claim: The great majority of commentators understand al-Haqqa to mean the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu hâkka kelimesine “kıyamet” anlamı vermiş

rows.speaker: Ateş
rows.claim: Some instead connect al-Haqqa with the crushing defeat that would befall Quraysh for opposing the Prophet, prompted by the following mention of punished peoples.
rows.anchor: dünyada azaba uğramış kavimlerin anılmasından hareketle hâkka kelimesinden, Hz. Peygamber’e isyan eden Kureyş’in başına gelecek olan ağır yenilgiye dikkat çekildiği görüşünde olanlar da vardır (Ateş

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God explained the paths of guidance and error, good and evil, as also stated in Beled 90:10.
rows.anchor: Biz insana hidâyet ve dalâlet, hayır ve şer yollarını açıklayarak gideceği yolu gösterdik

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God explained the paths of happiness and misery.
rows.anchor: Mutluluk ve mutsuzluk yollarını açıkladık

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that God created people with the capacity to understand their profit and loss.
rows.anchor: Kâr ve zararını anlayacak yetenekte yarattık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people rational, free, and able to distinguish good from evil; through prophets and revelation He showed the right way and gave them choice, so gratitude or ingratitude depends on how they use their capacities.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ insanı akıllı, iradeli ve iyiyi kötüden ayırma kabiliyetine sahip değerli bir varlık olarak yaratmış; görevlendirdiği peygamberler ve indirdiği vahiyle ona doğru yolu göstermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is an idiom of condemnation meaning great harm, evil, grief, punishment, or destruction.
rows.anchor: “Vay haline!” diye çevirdiğimiz veyl kelimesi, “ağır zarar, kötülük, hüzün, azap, helâk” gibi anlamlara gelen

rows.speaker: hadisler
rows.claim: Hadith reports also describe Wayl as the name of a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: hadislerde cehennemdeki bir vadinin ismi olduğu da bildirilmiştir

rows.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
rows.claim: Raghib says the valley meaning is figurative: those addressed by wayl will suffer Hell's punishment.
rows.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî’ye göre bu kelimenin cehennemdeki bir vadiye isim verilmesi, mecazi anlamda olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutaffifin is the plural of mutaffif: people who take full or extra measure when receiving but give short measure when selling.
rows.anchor: “alırken fazla fazla, verirken eksik ölçenler” mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses condemn short measure and warn of punishment; measuring is an example of the wider duty to honor responsibilities as carefully as rights and uphold truth and justice in all dealings.
rows.anchor: ölçü ve tartı örnek bir işlem olup daha genel olarak insanların, kendi haklarını gözettikleri kadar sorumluluklarını da özenle yerine getirmeleri gerektiği vurgulanmakta

rows.speaker: Ebü’l-Kāsım el-Kuşeyrî
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri gives a similar general interpretation of the duty to honor rights and responsibilities.
rows.anchor: Ebü’l-Kāsım el-Kuşeyrî’nin bu yöndeki bir yorumu için bk. Râzî

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Medinans cheated in measure when the Prophet arrived; after these verses were revealed, they corrected their practice.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan şöyle bir rivayet naklederler: Hz. Peygamber Medine’ye geldiği zaman Medineliler ölçü ve tartıda hile yapıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers reading the report as the Prophet reciting earlier Meccan verses after seeing some Medinan merchants cheat, rather than treating the report as the verses' original occasion.
rows.anchor: bu rivayeti, Resûlullah’ın, Medine’ye geldiği zaman ticaretle uğraşan birtakım insanların ölçü ve tartıyı eksik yaptıklarını görünce, daha önce Mekke döneminde inmiş olan bu âyetleri onlara tebliğ ettiği şeklinde anlamak daha isabetli olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the occasion was specific, the warning applies generally to dishonesty in work and trade, selfishness, and deceiving others.
rows.anchor: genel anlamda iş ve ticaret hayatında doğruluk ve dürüstlükten sapmanın çirkinliğine dikkat çekilmiş, bencillik ve başkalarını aldatma gibi ahlâka aykırı duygu ve davranış içinde olanlar kınanıp uyarılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commands to measure justly occur in Enam 6:152, Isra 17:35, and Rahman 55:8-9; violating them brings divine condemnation in this life and severe punishment in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Ölçü ve tartının adaletle yapılmasını emreden başka âyetler de vardır (meselâ bk. En‘âm 6/152; İsrâ 17/35; Rahmân 55/8-9)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cheaters would not dare such fraud if they firmly believed, or even considered it possible, that they would be resurrected.
rows.anchor: bunu muhtemel görmeleri halinde bile bu sahtekârlığa cüret etmelerinin mümkün olmadığına dikkat çekilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day is the Resurrection, when resurrection, judgment, punishment, and entry into Paradise or Hell take place.
rows.anchor: 5. âyette ifade edilen “büyük gün”den maksat kıyamet günüdür. Öldükten sonra dirilme, hesap, ceza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people will be resurrected and brought before the Lord of the worlds for judgment; no evil will remain hidden and each deed will be accounted for.
rows.anchor: o gün bütün insanların hesaba çekilmek üzere diriltilip âlemlerin rabbinin huzuruna çıkarılacakları ifade buyurularak uhrevî yargı ve hesap sırasında hiçbir kimsenin hiçbir kötülüğünün gizli kalmayacağı

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Some read insan as humanity generally because these negative traits occur to some degree in everyone.
rows.anchor: “insan” kavramıyla genel olarak insan türünün kastedildiği, çünkü bütün insanlarda bu tür olumsuz özelliklerin az çok bulunduğu belirtildiği gibi (bk. İbn Âşûr

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Another view is that insan especially means people who have not received guidance; Razi says this is the majority view.
rows.anchor: Râzî, bu ikinci yorumun çoğunluğun görüşü olduğunu belirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses describe ingrained ingratitude for God's gifts, disregard for gratitude, attachment to hoarding wealth, and failure to fulfill the duty of thankfulness.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın nimetlerine karşı nankörlük, kadir bilmezlik, mal biriktirmeye düşkünlük ve nimetin şükrünü yerine getirme vecîbesini umursamama gibi olumsuz özellikleri

rows.speaker: hadis
rows.claim: A hadith explains kanud as a person who eats alone, beats his enslaved person, and neglects financial obligations.
rows.anchor: bir hadiste şöyle açıklandığı rivayet edilir: “Öyle bir nankördür ki yalnız başına yer, kölesini döver, malî görevlerini yerine getirmez”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can say that people themselves recognize their ingratitude and that their own conscience bears witness to it; this best fits the context.
rows.anchor: insanın kendisinin de bu nankörlüğünün farkında olduğunu, buna bizzat kendi vicdanının da tanıklık ettiğini belirtmektedir

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: The verse is also interpreted as meaning that God is witness to this ingratitude, which warns the ungrateful.
rows.anchor: Âyete “Şüphesiz buna Allah şahittir” mânası da verilmiştir (Taberî, XXX, 180)

rows.speaker: Elmalılı
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the ungrateful person will testify against himself in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Âyete ayrıca “Nankör kişi âhirette kendi aleyhine şahitlik edecektir” şeklinde de mâna verilebilir (Elmalılı

rows.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
rows.claim: Hayr can mean things people generally desire, such as reason, justice, virtue, or something beneficial.
rows.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî, “akıl, adalet, fazilet, faydalı nesne gibi genellikle insanların rağbet ettiği şey” şeklinde tarif etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancient Arabs often used hayr for wealth and especially horses; here it means abundant wealth.
rows.anchor: Eski Araplar’da kelime sıklıkla “mal” ve özellikle “at” anlamında kullanılmaktaydı. Burada “çok mal, servet” mânasında kullanıldığı anlaşılmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl can mean severe punishment, destruction, disgrace, a valley in Hell, or a curse; the rendering vay haline signals these senses.
rows.anchor: “Vay haline!” diye çevirdiğimiz veyl kelimesi “çetin azap, helâk, yok olma, rezil rüsvâ olma, cehennemde bir vadi, beddua” anlamlarına gelmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humaza means habitual backbiting, mocking by gesture, or humiliating people and injuring their honor and dignity.
rows.anchor: “birini arkasından çekiştirmek, kaş göz, el kol işaretleriyle onunla alay etmek, aşağılamak” mânalarına gelen hemz kökünden türemiş bir sıfat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lumaza describes the same fault shown to a person's face rather than behind their back.
rows.anchor: lümeze kelimesi de benzer davranışları arkadan değil, kişinin yüzüne karşı gösteren kimseyi ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verses were revealed about the pagan Arab Ahnes b. Shurayq, who boasted of his wealth and mocked people, damaging their character.
rows.anchor: mal ve servetinin çokluğuyla gururlanıp insanlarla alay ederek onların şahsiyetlerini zedeleyen Ahnes b. Şüreyk isimli putperest Arap hakkında indiği rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specific occasion does not limit the ruling: Islam protects personal dignity, condemns these behaviors, and warns that their practitioners face punishment by fire in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: sûrenin iniş sebebinin özel olması hükmünün genel olmasına engel değildir. İslâm dini, insan şahsiyetinin ve onurunun korunmasına son derece önem verdiği için Kur’an bu tür davranışları kınamakta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant mockers also amass wealth without regard for lawful limits, hoard it from fear of poverty, withhold charity and the poor's due, and imagine wealth makes them immortal.
rows.anchor: helâl haram demeden mal toplayan, onu saklayan, fakirlik korkusuyla cimrilik ederek onu hayır yolunda harcamaktan kaçınan, fakirin hakkını vermeyen ve servetinin kendisini ebedîleştireceğini sanan

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports, through a chain called sound, that Medinans cheated most in measure when the Prophet arrived; after the verse, they measured properly.
rows.anchor: بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس قال لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا أبخس الناس كيلا فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter is Medinan, with no disagreement reported.
rows.anchor: مدنية بلا خلاف

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says al-Baqara was the first surah revealed in Medina.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: أول سورة أنزلت بالمدينة سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid divides the opening passage into four verses about believers, two about disbelievers, and thirteen about hypocrites.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: أربع آيات من أول هذه السورة نزلت في المؤمنين، وآيتان بعدها نزلتا في الكافرين، وثلاث عشرة بعدها نزلت في المنافقين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse about disbelievers was revealed about Abu Jahl and five members of his household.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: نزلت في أبي جهل وخمسة من أهل بيته

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi instead says the disbelievers meant here are the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Abdullah b. Ubayy and his companions: he warmly praised Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali before believers, then told his followers to imitate him and mock them; the Muslims reported this to the Prophet, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه، وذلك أنهم خرجوا ذات يوم فاستقبلهم نفر من أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Jews who told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to follow Judaism when he died.
rows.anchor: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات أوصى بنيه باليهودية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns leading Jews of Medina and Christians of Najran, who disputed with Muslims and each claimed its prophet, scripture, and religion were superior while rejecting Jesus and the Gospel or Muhammad and the Quran; both urged Muslims to convert.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في رؤوس يهود المدينة: كعب بن الأشرف، ومالك بن الصيف، ووهب بن يهوذا، وأبي ياسر ابن أخطب

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that a man from Taif died in Medina, leaving parents, children, and a wife; the Prophet allocated shares to the parents and children but none to the wife, and ordered them to maintain her for a year.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية: أن رجلا من أهل الطائف قدم المدينة وله أولاد رجال ونساء، ومعه أبواه وامرأته، فمات بالمدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some Ansar mothers vowed to Judaize any child who survived; after Banu Nadir were expelled and Ansar children were among them, the Ansar wanted to keep their children, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كانت المرأة من نساء الأنصار تكون مقلاة فتجعل على نفسها إن عاش لها ولد أن تهوده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr explains that the children could either join the expelled group or enter Islam.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: فمن شاء لحق بهم ومن شاء دخل في الإسلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about an Ansari man who tried to force his black enslaved boy Subayh to convert to Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار كان له غلام أسود يقال له: صبيح وكان يكرهه على الإسلام

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that Banu Amr b. Umayr demanded their principal from Banu al-Mughira, who pleaded hardship and asked for time until the crop came in; they refused, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: قالت بنو عمرو بن عمير لبني المغيرة: هاتوا رؤوس أموالنا ولكن الربا ندعه لكم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that revelation of 2:284 distressed the Companions, who said they could manage prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity but not this burden; the Prophet told them to hear and obey, and after they did, 2:285-286 followed and abrogated 2:284.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لما أنزل على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} الآية، اشتد ذلك على أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Companions felt distress at 2:284; after the Prophet told them to hear, obey, and submit, God placed faith in their hearts, then revealed 2:286, whose pleas God answered.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} دخل قلوبهم منها شيء

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama says that in the Prophet's time there was no campaign requiring frontier garrison duty; the verse's murabata meant waiting for one prayer after another.
rows.anchor: قال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: يا ابن أخي هل تدري في أي شيء نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Thabit b. Rifa'a and his uncle: after Rifa'a died leaving a young son, the uncle asked the Prophet what he could use from the boy's property and when he should hand it over.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ثابت بن رفاعة وفي عمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفي وترك ابنه ثابتا وهو صغير

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say Aws b. Thabit's cousins and executors took his estate, leaving his wife Umm Kujja and three daughters without support; they followed a custom of inheriting only for adult men who fought, and argued the daughters could not ride or fight. The Prophet deferred judgment until revelation came.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن أوس بن ثابت الأنصاري توفي وترك امرأة يقال لها: أم كجة وثلاث بنات له منها، فقام رجلان

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the verse concerns believers whom God had told the Prophet not to turn away; the Prophet greeted them first and praised God for commanding him to do so.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: نزلت في الذين نهى الله تعالى نبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن طردهم

rows.speaker: ماهان الحنفي
rows.claim: Mahan al-Hanafi says people came to the Prophet confessing grave sins; after they left without an apparent response, this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال ماهان الحنفي: أتى قوم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالوا: إنا أصبنا ذنوبا عظاما

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse concerns al-Nadr b. al-Harith and Quraysh leaders, who mockingly demanded the punishment Muhammad had promised.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في النضر بن الحارث ورؤساء قريش، كانوا يقولون: يا محمد ائتنا بالعذاب الذي تعدنا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Walibi's transmission, says Jews asked Muhammad whether God had sent him a book; when he said yes, they swore God had sent no book from heaven, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي: قالت اليهود: يا محمد، أنزل الله عليك كتابا؟

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad b. Ka'b says God commanded Muhammad to ask the People of the Book how they found him in their scriptures; envy made them reject God's book and Messenger and claim no scripture was sent to any human.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: أمر الله محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يسأل أهل الكتاب عن أمره

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr reports that the Jewish scholar Malik b. al-Sayf, angered when asked whether the Torah said God hates a fat rabbi, denied revelation to any human—even Moses—and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: جاء رجل من اليهود يقال له مالك بن الصيف، فخاصم النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about parents urging their child to associate partners with God was revealed concerning Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas, as also recounted in Surat al-Ankabut.
rows.anchor: نزلت في سعد بن أبي وقاص على ما ذكرناه في سورة العنكبوت

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ataa reports from Ibn Abbas that follow the path of one who turns to God was revealed about Abu Bakr: after Abu Bakr affirmed belief in Muhammad, Abd al-Rahman b. Awf, Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas, Sa'id b. Zayd, Uthman, Talha, and al-Zubayr also believed.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد أبا بكر، وذلك أنه حين أسلم أتاه عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say Jews first asked about the spirit, prompting 17:85; after migration they challenged the claim of limited knowledge against the Torah's scope and the Quran's description of wisdom as great good, and 31:27 was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: سألت اليهود رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الروح، فأنزل الله بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Medinans were especially dishonest in measuring when the Prophet arrived; after the verse was revealed, they measured correctly.
rows.anchor: أن عكرمة حدثه عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi says Medinan merchants used deceptive sales resembling games of chance, including munabadha, mulamasa, and mukhatara; the Prophet went to the market and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال القرظي: كان بالمدينة تجار يطففون، وكانت بياعاتهم كشبه القمار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerned Abu Juhayna, who had two measuring vessels, using one to measure out and another to measure in.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: قدم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المدينة وبها رجل يقال له:
